title: Paramartha Guru Tale 98

full_text:
A night burglar entered the ashram kitchen, stole two brass pots, but in his haste to squeeze through the window, his red cotton turban caught on an iron nail and remained hanging on the sill.

Next morning, Matti found the red turban: 'Master! The thief escaped, but his headpiece was captured!'

Guru Paramartha convened a court on the veranda.

The red turban was placed upon a wooden stool.

Madayan addressed the turban: 'Accused Turban! You were caught at the scene of the burglary! Where are the two stolen brass pots?'

The turban remained motionless.

'Contempt of court!' roared the Guru. 'Sentence the accused to twenty lashes of the cane!'

The disciples beat the red turban with bamboo switches until it was frayed to threads.

Then, Guru Paramartha sentenced the turban to imprisonment: 'Lock the turban in the iron trunk for seven years!'

They locked the battered turban in the chest, proud of their swift justice, while the real thief sold the two brass pots in the next village for four rupees.
moral: Arresting a turban for a burglary lets the thief walk away with the loot.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Paramartha Guru Tale 98"?
options: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
